ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Irène Joliot-Curie Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: New patient visit for two months of tiredness, bruising and bleeding gums: blood count with blasts on the smear, and urgent hematology referral. Concerns: She has been worn out for two months, bruises easily and her gums bleed; she suspects her blood and wants to know at once; She knows the long-term effects of radiation on the bone marrow from her own field and from her mother's illness, and wants her exposure history taken seriously. [S]

tr.td: Worked as a nurse radiographer with X-ray machines in field hospitals in the First World War, the start of her occupational radiation exposure
Tuberculosis, with a long recovery in Switzerland during the Second World War
A capsule of polonium exploded on her laboratory bench
Health visibly declining from shortly after this year

list.item: Two months of tiredness, easy bruising and bleeding gums, with pancytopenia and 12 percent blasts on the blood smear; acute leukemia suspected and urgent hematology review booked: resolved, confirmed [S]

Acute myeloid leukemia diagnosed on bone marrow biopsy (34 percent myeloblasts), in a physicist with decades of occupational exposure to ionizing radiation; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to her documented leukemia: active, confirmed [S]

Occupational exposure to ionizing radiation over about four decades: X-ray work early in her career, laboratory work with polonium and other radioactive sources, and a laboratory accident in which a sealed polonium source ruptured on her bench about ten years ago: active, confirmed [S]
Pulmonary tuberculosis in her forties, treated to completion; no symptoms of active disease: active, confirmed [S]

Moderately reduced lung gas transfer (DLCO 58 percent of predicted, FEV1 76 percent) from old tuberculous scarring of the right upper lobe; with performance status 2, it makes her unfit for intensive induction: active, confirmed [S]
Nausea with vomiting and constipation on day 11 of cycle 1 of azacitidine with venetoclax, without fever, with mild low potassium; managed as an outpatient; resolved: resolved, confirmed [S]

tr.td: New patient visit for two months of tiredness, bruising and bleeding gums: blood count with blasts on the smear, and urgent hematology referral
Hematology consultation and bone marrow biopsy: diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia, transfusion, and pre-treatment work-up
Genetic results, classification and risk, fitness for treatment, early palliative care, and day 1 of azacitidine with venetoclax
Day 22 of cycle 1: bone marrow response, transfusion and infection review, and stopping venetoclax for count recovery
Count recovery and response assessment; cycle 2; transplant evaluation; occupational dose records
Same-day sick visit for nausea, vomiting and constipation during cycle 1
Periodic adult preventive visit during AML therapy

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Urgent evaluation of pancytopenia with blasts on the smear: peripheral smear review, comprehensive metabolic panel, LDH and uric acid today; coagulation tests at the hematology visit; no aspirin or anti-inflammatory drugs; go to the emergency department at once for a temperature of 38.0 °C or more, bleeding that does not stop, or new confusion or headache
Urgent hematology/oncology consultation within two days for suspected acute leukemia: bone marrow biopsy, classification and treatment plan

Occupational health history: her work with X-rays, polonium and other sources over about four decades, and the sealed-source accident in her laboratory, documented; written request to the employer's radiation safety office for her dosimetry and bioassay records, which the employer must keep and must furnish on request

Transfusion support: irradiated, leukoreduced products; red cells one unit at a time for hemoglobin below 7 to 8 g/dL or symptoms; platelets for a count below 10 x10^3/uL, for bleeding, or before procedures that need them

Pre-treatment work-up: HLA typing for a future transplant, hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV testing, chest X-ray because of past tuberculosis, echocardiogram, lung function tests with diffusing capacity, and a dental check

Induction with azacitidine 75 mg/m2 on days 1 to 7 and venetoclax ramped up to 70 mg daily (the dose for use with posaconazole), in 28-day cycles; admitted for the ramp-up with tumor lysis monitoring, allopurinol and fluids; bone marrow at day 21 to 28, holding venetoclax if blasts are below 5% until counts recover; later cycles with 21 days of venetoclax

Infection prevention: posaconazole, acyclovir, and levofloxacin while neutrophils are below 0.5; a written fever plan (temperature of 38.0 °C or more: go to the emergency department for antibiotics within one hour); hand hygiene and food safety
Specialist palliative care alongside treatment from the first cycle: symptoms, prognosis in plain numbers, her goals and values, and advance care planning, reviewed at every visit

Allogeneic stem cell transplant evaluation by the transplant center from the first cycle: an unrelated donor search from her HLA typing, reduced-intensity conditioning if she reaches remission, and measurable residual disease monitoring

Nausea and constipation during cycle 1: ondansetron as needed after a normal QTc, with no other QT-prolonging antiemetic; polyethylene glycol and senna by mouth, no rectal medicines while neutropenic; potassium replaced; red cells and platelets given; venetoclax continued with food
Diagnosis, classification and a treatment decision within two weeks of the first visit
Marrow two days after the first visit; genetics back and treatment started on day 14
Complete cycle 1 without tumor lysis, invasive fungal infection, or bleeding
No tumor lysis; no fever or fungal infection; no bleeding beyond bruising; one outpatient visit for nausea
Remission on the response assessment after cycle 1 (ELN 2022 complete remission, or complete remission with partial hematologic recovery)
Day-22 marrow blasts 3%; at day 33 neutrophils 0.9 and platelets 88: complete remission with partial hematologic recovery, measurable residual disease positive
Her own goals and values recorded and her symptoms controlled with the palliative care team from the first cycle
Seen by the palliative care team on day 1; goals recorded; symptoms reviewed at every visit
Her occupational dose records obtained and the exposure history documented
Records requested in writing from the employer's radiation safety office; history documented
